entries.opening: This one is about the connector's sign-in, not your social accounts.

steps.text: invalid_grant here means your Blotato MCP sign-in expired.

cite.quote: Your Blotato MCP OAuth connection expired.

steps.text: First, log into your Blotato account in your browser. The approval needs it.

cite.quote: Make sure you are logged into your Blotato account in the browser. The OAuth approval requires an active Blotato session.

steps.text: Then in Claude, open Customize > Connectors, remove the Blotato connector, add it again, and approve access.

cite.quote: In Claude, open Customize > Connectors, remove and re-add the Blotato custom connector, and re-approve access via OAuth.

steps.text: The Fix My Automation button will not help with this one. It only works for n8n.

cite.quote: it does not work for Make.com, Claude, MCP, or direct REST API calls.

entries.next: Re-add the connector, then ask Claude to list your Blotato accounts.
entries.proof: You will know it worked when Claude answers with your account list. An empty list still counts: it means no social accounts are connected yet.

entries.title: Asking an AI tool to edit a scheduled post made a second post
phrasings: I asked Claude to change the caption on a scheduled post and it made a second one
my AI agent was supposed to update the post but it created a new one
editing a scheduled post through MCP made a duplicate
why did ChatGPT create another post when I only wanted an edit
how do I edit a scheduled post with Claude without making a copy
Claude made a new post instead of changing the old one
I told my agent to move the post time and the post shows twice
mcp edit created a duplicate post
the connector in claude doubled my post when I fixed a word
not_this: my post was published twice on instagram
you are not allowed to create a tweet with duplicate content
the blotato connector in claude says invalid_grant
entries.opening: This one has a known cause, and a short instruction for your AI tool.

steps.text: To edit a scheduled post, the AI tool should call only blotato_update_schedule. It changes the existing schedule and never makes a new post.

cite.quote: It updates an existing schedule in place — it never creates a new post.

steps.text: Two posts for what should have been an edit most likely means the AI tool also called blotato_create_post.

cite.quote: If you ever see two posts published for what should have been an edit, your AI tool likely also called `blotato_create_post`.

steps.text: Tell it in so many words: use only blotato_update_schedule, and do not create a new post.

cite.quote: Tell it explicitly: "use only `blotato_update_schedule`, do not create a new post."

steps.text: To change the caption or media, it has to pass the whole post, not only the part you are changing.

cite.quote: To change the caption or media: pass the **whole `post` object**, not just the field you're editing.

entries.next: Tell your AI tool to use only blotato_update_schedule for edits, and not to create a new post.
entries.proof: You will know it worked when your next edit changes the scheduled post and no second post shows in the calendar.
